A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–Q support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original vector and neuron interventions, multilingual value evaluations, response-diversity measurements, jailbreak experiments, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains extensive original experimental results and additionally reports a Persona-only jailbreak comparison and baseline-versus-steering correlations.

M1.justification: The vector-extraction and steering approach remains, but the stated neuron-selection rule changes. v2 Section 2.2 permits unique neurons within 60° of a difference-axis direction; v3 Section 3.2 requires alignment within 30° of the closest shared or unique axis. The PDFs do not establish whether corresponding experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The explicit value-suppressing prompt scenario reported alongside positive prompts in v2 Section 4.3 is absent from v3. Otherwise, the conversational corpora, value benchmarks, five evaluation languages, jailbreak benchmarks, GAMBIT, and IFEval coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 25 adds Persona, meaning the system prompt without steering, to the jailbreak comparison. v2 Table 26 lacks this comparator. GCG, PAIR, TAP, DR, Human, and DSN remain, as do the existing probe and random-baseline comparisons elsewhere.

E3.justification: The jailbreak comparison gains an explicit system-prompt-only control, while the positive/negative-prompt PVQ testing procedure is removed. The principal PVQ formats, intervention grid search, decoding sweeps, and jailbreak budgets of 520/400 queries and nine system prompts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix F.5 adds a baseline-versus-steering correlation analysis and a Benevolence case study. It removes v2 Appendix A.5's shared-axis stability analysis and Section 4.3's opposite-prompt compliance check. Token-span ablations, probe comparisons, implicit-prompt controls, and base-model experiments are retained.

E5.justification: The 51-resample shared-axis bootstrap analysis and its confidence intervals are removed. v3 Appendix F.5 adds Pearson correlations with p < 0.001. Human-agreement uncertainty, diversity permutation tests, Procrustes bootstrap intervals, and five-seed jailbreak confidence reporting remain.

E6.justification: v3 adds EAD entries in Table 2, four Persona baseline ASRs in Table 25, and correlations of −0.6605 and −0.7443 in Appendix F.5. Lexical-entropy values also change between v2 Figure 8 and v3 Figure 9. Bootstrap and opposite-prompt findings are removed. Most benchmark tables retain their numbers; revised headline jailbreak percentages select summary values already present in v2.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.2 explicitly defines signed unique axes, revises their angular membership condition, and adds a formal decomposition of MLP residual updates into neuron contributions. The difference-in-means and orthogonalization mathematics are retained, including equations moved from the appendix.

C1.justification: Both versions claim partially shared intrinsic and prompted mechanisms, greater prompted steerability, greater intrinsic response diversity, and prompted-unique instruction compliance. v3 foregrounds existing multilingual and Schwartz-geometry findings without materially changing the central contributions.

C2.justification: The tentative baseline-ceiling explanation in v2 Section 3.2.2 becomes a stronger interpretation in v3 Appendix F.5: smaller gains are attributed to existing alignment rather than ineffective vectors. v3 Section 5.3 also explicitly hypothesizes suppression of safety alignment or alternative views. Existing capability boundaries and Appendix O's training-dynamics account remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents top-k-percent magnitude filtering, giving 15% as an example, and explicitly includes layer normalization in vocabulary projection. Its release statement promises code and dataset, replacing v2's promise of MIT-licensed source code. These are disclosure changes; neither PDF provides newly available released resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds pluralistic-alignment positioning and references including Sorensen, Castricato, and Lake. It removes discussion of SAE-denoised steering, dense instruction steering, and spectral-method precedents accompanying the deleted stability analysis. The central positioning between intrinsic and prompted value research remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, and results narrative are substantially rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 5 to Section 2; extraction equations move into the main method; human validation and implicit-prompt descriptions are reorganized across appendices. These changes substantially reshape the exposition.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column layout. v3 adds a neuron-geometry figure, labels pipeline stages, replaces detailed main-text benchmark plots with aggregate displays while retaining detailed plots in Appendix F, and redraws the entropy chart. Tables gain EAD and Persona columns, alongside extensive resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: v3 offers clearer methodological exposition, an informative Persona-only control, and a new baseline-constraint analysis. However, it removes shared-axis bootstrap validation and opposite-prompt compliance evidence. It also retains neuron results while tightening the documented selection rule without explaining their relationship. These gains coexist with lost validation and unresolved methodological consistency, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
